what: for finding 035: what can the postcondition selection be read back AS, and what does the HTML flavour really contain?
why: the readback's closed tag set was written to fit the fixtures rather than documents, so it rejects <b>/<i> and -- because the serialiser wraps every CJK run in <font><span> -- every paragraph of a Chinese document. odfdom's answer to the same classification problem is to generate it from the ODF RelaxNG schema (paragraph-content alone has 163 refs) and to keep a tiny set of structural roots (nine elements declare isComponentRoot). That says a hand-written inline allowlist is the wrong shape, and raises the question this probe measures: is a format with a schema reachable at all?
candidateListProvenance: derived from source, not guessed: SwTransferable::SetDataForDragAndDrop adds EMBED_SOURCE, RTF, RICHTEXT, HTML, MARKDOWN, STRING for a text selection (sw/source/uibase/dochdl/swdtflvr.cxx:3734-3746); mime strings from sot/source/base/exchange.cxx:136,200.

answer1_canWeReadOdf.shortAnswer: yes, but only through getClipboard, and at a price

getTextSelection.reading: PK\x03\x04 -- a ZIP, i.e. the real ODF package. strlen stops at 5 because byte 6 is NUL. convertOString memcpy's the whole payload and tolerates NULs (init.cxx:377), but getTextSelection returns no length, so the caller cannot know where the data ends. Reachable in principle, unusable through this API.

getClipboard.note: pMimeTypes=NULL makes core enumerate getTransferDataFlavors() (init.cxx:6082) -- the offer measured rather than listed by us. It reads the LOK clipboard, so .uno:Copy must run first.

negativeControl.why: a plausible-looking ODF mime type that appears nowhere in the exchange table. It fails, so a run where everything else succeeds is distinguishable from a probe that cannot report failure.

costOfTakingIt: the payload is a ZIP: the engine would need to unpack content.xml in WASM

getClipboard reads the clipboard, so every format action would have to dispatch .uno:Copy and clobber the user's clipboard -- a visible side effect worse than the caret move route C already has to restore

answer2_htmlTagInventory.shortAnswer: the structural/inline split odfdom uses does hold here, on this corpus
answer2_htmlTagInventory.method: every open tag recorded with its nesting context across 17 anchors in 6 fixtures; a tag seen at body level cannot be ignored by a rule that says 'ignore anything inside an open block'
answer2_htmlTagInventory.violations: none -- b, i, font and span appeared only inside an already-open block, never at body level
answer2_htmlTagInventory.boundedBy:
the corpus. No hyperlink, footnote, comment anchor or inline image appeared inside a probed paragraph, and table/td never appeared at all (SelectText inside a table cell serialises as a bare

). 'No violations' is evidence over the shapes measured, not a proof over ODF.

answer3_markdown.shortAnswer: text/markdown expresses all five closed actions, and the finding 035 defect does not exist in it
answer3_markdown.whyItMatters: Markdown has no font runs, so the CJK wrapper that breaks the HTML read has nothing to correspond to. The postcondition would stop needing a tag classification at all.

acrossParagraphShapes.inline-formatted: - Normal **bold anchor** and *italic anchor*. -- same prefixes, inline markers inside
acrossParagraphShapes.cjk: - 第二段中文 beta -- NO wrapper of any kind, where HTML writes <font face="DejaVu Sans"><span lang="zh-TW">

answer3_markdown.twoAxesStillSeparate: listTag from the leading '- ' / '1. ' / neither; blockTag from the leading '# ' / neither. The same split the HTML read already makes, and the same narrowing (heading-ness is answerable, 'Text body vs default' is not).

multiBlockSignature.singleParagraph: '- E1-STYLED-END\n' -- one trailing newline, no blank line
multiBlockSignature.selectAll:
'# E1-STYLED-HEADING

Normal **bold anchor** and *italic anchor*.

- E1-LIST-ONE

- E1-LIST-TWO

E1-STYLED-END
'
multiBlockSignature.reading: blocks are separated by a blank line, so finding 034's multi-block guard survives the change: 'the payload contains \n\n' replaces 'more than one block tag'.

notMeasured: hyperlinks, footnotes, comment anchors and inline images inside a selected paragraph -- absent from the corpus, so the tag inventory's 'no violations' is bounded by that
whether a hard line break inside a paragraph emits \n\n and so trips the multi-block guard (fails closed, so the safe direction, but unmeasured)

whether the Markdown export is stable across versions -- it is a serialiser output with no documented contract, the same objection SPEC E2-A 2.8 already records against the HTML read. The exposed surface is three tokens instead of an open tag set, which is smaller, not zero.

answer4_markdownEscaping.shortAnswer: PARTIAL, and the half that is missing is the half that matters -- the Markdown route is refused
answer4_markdownEscaping.why: the whole route rests on a plain paragraph never reading back as a list item or heading. The exporter escapes three of the five characters and not the other two.
answer4_markdownEscaping.fixture: markdown-syntax: each look-alike paired with the real thing, because the question is whether the two can be told apart, not what either produces alone

notEscaped.- MD-DASH is a plain paragraph: - MD-DASH is a plain paragraph  (hex 2d20 -- a bare '- ')

theCollision.realListItem: - MD-REAL-ITEM is a real list item\n
theCollision.reading: byte-identical in shape. A paragraph whose text merely begins with '- ' is indistinguishable from a bulleted list item, so set-list-unordered would read back as satisfied on a paragraph that never joined a list. That is a false POSITIVE -- the direction the whole barrier exists to prevent. Same for '1. ' and ordered lists. The heading axis is safe ('#' is escaped), but one safe axis does not rescue the design.

theRescueThatWasConsideredAndRefused.mechanism: text/plain does NOT carry the marker for a real list item ('MD-REAL-ITEM is a real list item') while text/markdown does, so markdown-minus-plain recovers the marker and would in principle discriminate.
whyRefused: it needs two reads and a prefix-subtraction rule made fragile by the escape backslashes and the trailing newline
it depends on the escaping being incomplete. If upstream fixes the exporter to write '\\-', the subtraction silently changes meaning -- building on a bug and calling it a contract

answer4_markdownEscaping.upstreamNote: the Markdown export escapes #, > and * at the start of a paragraph but not - or 1., so its own output does not round-trip: exporting a plain paragraph beginning '- ' and reimporting yields a list item. Not searched for duplicates, not reported. Low priority, same standing as the SwWrtShell::SelPara note in finding 034.

decision.chosen: HTML with an odfdom-shaped structural classification (option B)
decision.markdown: REFUSED on the escaping measurement above -- not on taste
decision.odf: REFUSED on cost: reachable only through getClipboard, which means clobbering the user's clipboard on every format action and unpacking a ZIP inside the WASM engine
decision.structuralTagsFromMeasurement: p, h1, ul, ol, li -- the tags observed at body level across 17 anchors, plus ol which the action sweep produces. Everything inside an open block is ignored; an unknown STRUCTURAL tag still fails closed.
decision.openForDecision:
whether to include table/td/h2-h6/blockquote. They never appeared: SelectText inside a table cell serialises as a bare

, and the closed action set has one heading level. Adding them now would be listing from imagination rather than measurement, which is what this probe exists to avoid.
